memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "The Lord will deliver them to you, and you must do to them all that I have commanded you. Be strong and courageous. Do not be afraid or terrified because of them, for the Lord your God goes with you; he will never leave you nor forsake you." — Deut 31:5-6 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here are some of the most treasured words in all of Scripture: "Be strong and courageous. Do not be afraid... for the Lord your God goes with you; he will never leave you nor forsake you." Notice that the command to be courageous is not a demand to summon strength from within ourselves by sheer willpower. The courage is rooted in a promise — the promise of God's unfailing presence. We can be brave because He is with us.

This is how biblical courage works. It is not the absence of fear or pretending danger isn't real. It is facing real challenges while holding onto a real presence — the presence of the God who never leaves. The people had every human reason to be afraid of the powerful nations ahead. But their courage rested not on their own strength but on the God who goes with them.

That promise — "he will never leave you nor forsake you" — is one God repeats throughout Scripture. The writer of Hebrews quotes these very words to New Testament believers, adding, "So we say with confidence, 'The Lord is my helper; I will not be afraid'" (Heb 13:5-6). This promise is yours in Christ.

Whatever you are facing today, you do not face it alone. The God who has promised never to leave you is with you in it. Let that presence be the ground of your courage. You can be strong, not because you are strong, but because He is with you and will never let you go.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where do I need courage today, and what is my courage resting on?
2. How does the promise "he will never leave you" change my fear?
3. What challenge can I face differently, knowing God is with me?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that You will never leave me nor forsake me. When I am afraid, remind me of Your unfailing presence. Make me strong and courageous, not in myself, but in You. Amen.
